gate: verbatim: 'a test-isolation pass first - any test writing a repo-root store races under -n; store_lock covers .self_embeddings.json, the others are unaudited.'
row_source_for: the grouping step: `xdist_group` per file, consumed by `pytest -n auto --dist loadgroup`. Rows are truth — any prose restating this file is a render and goes stale when rows move.

empirical.what: a pytest plugin wrapping builtins.open, os.open/remove/unlink/mkdir/makedirs/rmdir/rename/replace/truncate, shutil.copy*/move/rmtree/copytree, Path.write_text/write_bytes/mkdir/touch/unlink/rmdir/rename/replace/symlink_to/chmod and subprocess.Popen, recording every path under the repo root attributed to the running nodeid. This is what catches the INDIRECT class — a test reaching a src function that writes a repo-root store by default — which no grep can see.
empirical.run_full: PYTHONPATH=<scratch> TRACER_OUT=<scratch>/full_trace.jsonl python3 -m pytest -q -p write_tracer -rfE   ->  3 failed, 4975 passed, 69 skipped, 24 xfailed in 514.35s; 1007 trace rows. THE SERIAL BASELINE for this gate.
empirical.run_recheck: same command over the 20 files whose rows were dir_fd-suspect, with the tracer corrected  ->  485 passed, 9 skipped, 6 xfailed in 95.36s; 111 trace rows.
empirical.correction: 516 of the first pass' 1007 rows were FALSE: shutil.rmtree walks with os.unlink(entry.name, dir_fd=fd), a BARE name that realpath() resolves against cwd (= the repo root). The corrected tracer skips any call carrying dir_fd. Fourteen files that looked unsafe are clean: test_editor_saves_store, test_evolution_consumer, test_evolve_gates, test_liveness, test_nodemap, test_operating_contract, test_pipeline_evolve, test_reconstruction_fence, test_section_bridge, test_soul_shard, test_superarc_genesis_loop, test_superarc_sequence_exec, test_w6_3_strip_and_drive, test_pipeline_surface (its only finding is the git index).
empirical.blind_spot: writes made INSIDE a subprocess are not traced — only the spawn is recorded, with its argv and cwd. Every subprocess seen at the live root is git plumbing; the mutating class (git add/commit/checkout) appears only against tmp repos.

method.static: AST scan of all test files: a name bound anywhere in a file to Path(__file__).resolve().parents[N] taints that name file-wide, and any write verb applied to it is a signature. Also chdir (ZERO hits in the whole tree) and raw os.environ mutation (ONE hit). Re-implemented in tests/test_xdist_isolation.py as the guard.

recommendation.why_not_load: plain --dist load distributes individual TESTS, so two tests in ONE file that share a fixed-name sentinel (test_scaffold_wipe, test_voice_conformance_detect, test_laplace) can run concurrently. Never use it here.
recommendation.why_not_loadfile: --dist loadfile pins a FILE to a worker, which closes every single-file store — but it does NOT honour xdist_group, so the two CROSS-file collisions (3 files on paper_falqon/manuscript/node_index.json; 5 files on the holdout score + .git/index) would still race.
recommendation.why_loadgroup: --dist loadgroup schedules like `load` but pins every test carrying the same xdist_group mark to one worker. Giving each needs-serialization file a group name — its shared store's name when it has one, its own path otherwise — reproduces loadfile's guarantee where it is needed and leaves the other {safe} files free to spread.
recommendation.wiring: a pytest_collection_modifyitems hook in tests/conftest.py reads THIS file and applies pytest.mark.xdist_group(name=row['xdist_group']) to every item whose file has one. Mechanical, so the rows stay the single source and no per-file marker edit can drift from them.

measured.serial: python3 -m pytest -q -rfE  ->  514.35s (4975 passed / 3 failed / 69 skipped / 24 xfailed). The 3 reds were the sibling lane's, and were already green again by the parallel run.
measured.parallel: python3 -m pytest -q -n auto --dist loadfile -rfE  ->  258.38s (5052 passed / 1 failed / 68 skipped / 24 xfailed) on 16 cores. SPEEDUP 1.99x, SAVING 256.0s per full suite.
measured.why_only_2x: --dist loadfile makes the LONGEST FILE the critical path, and this tree has a few very long ones (the playwright / in-process-server walks). The WO's 350-950s estimate assumed test-level spreading; 256s is what file-level pinning actually buys here. loadgroup restores test-level spreading for the ~305 ungrouped files, so it should land ABOVE this, not below.
measured.loadgroup_proof: the recommended wiring was RUN, not assumed: a pytest_collection_modifyitems hook reading this file's rows and applying pytest.mark.xdist_group(name=row['xdist_group']) -> `[group_hook] pinned 23 tests into 3 xdist_group(s)` at collection, and `pytest -q -p group_hook -n auto --dist loadgroup` over all 18 needs-serialization files -> 432 passed, 3 skipped in 46.04s, zero reds.
measured.isolation_reds: ZERO. None of the 15 needs-serialization files failed under -n. That is NOT proof they are safe — loadfile does not prevent the two cross-file collisions, they simply did not interleave on this run. The one red was the GPU class.

recommendation.dependency: pytest-xdist>=3.5 — already importable in this environment (importlib.metadata.version('pytest-xdist') == '3.8.0') but NOT declared. Declare it in pyproject.toml's [project.optional-dependencies] dev list, beside pytest/ruff/playwright.
residual_risks: git index: four files shell `git status --porcelain` at the live root; they are grouped together, but ANY sibling process (a concurrent sewup lane, an editor) can still dirty the tree under test_pipeline_surface's 'writes nothing' assertion. Parallelism does not create that coupling — it only makes it likelier.

order dependence: corpus_friction/suite_baseline.json names a historical order-dependent flake (test_bare_file_link_resolves_its_owning_corpus, tests/test_artefact_surface.py:68). -n reorders by construction, so the first parallel closes should watch for it.

_run() in scripts/sewup.py truncates pytest output to the last 2000 chars; with more workers the -rfE short summary is longer, so a very red run could have its FAILED lines cut before the harvest. Pre-existing, worth widening.
collection-time writes escape derived_writes.enabled() (PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST is unset during collection) in every mode, serial included.

known_reds_note: 3 reds against the EMPTY corpus_friction/suite_baseline.json. NOT caused by this audit's tracer and NOT a parallelism defect: they reproduce on a bare `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_design_conceptric.py` (3 failed, 9 passed in 3.58s) and are the sibling lane's in-flight scripts/build_design_conceptric.py + a grown corpus_friction/design-interface.jsonl.

rows.note: THE CLASS THE GREPS COULD NOT SEE, found by running the parallel suite: GPU VRAM is a contended resource, not a file. The card is 4096 MiB (nvidia-smi) and every worker that constructs a real FastEmbedBackend opens its own CUDA session. Load-dependent, not deterministic — it fired under the full 16-worker suite and not in a 13-file stress of the same files. Cure: one `device:gpu-vram` xdist_group so at most one worker holds a CUDA session.
